raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #64075.

_encode_local_features in deepseek_ocr.py and deepseek_ocr2.py used torch.sum(patches).item() == 0 to detect "no crop patches", so a tiled image whose normalized pixels cancel to zero (e.g. half-white/half-black 1536x768) wrongly returned None, dropped local features, and crashed EngineCore with a placeholder/embedding shape mismatch. Replace the guard with patches.numel() == 0; #59417 fixed the equivalent check in _parse_and_validate_image_input but left this one as "not engine-fatal", which #64075 disproves.

New test class TestDeepseekOCREncodeLocalFeaturesGuard fails on the base commit (2 failed) and passes with the fix (13 passed in tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_ocr.py); ruff check and ruff format are clean.

My [commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/709c30062cc7d3fa573427b02013c35e1e64577f) adds a `vllm_runner` regression test for that path.

I ran the tests on an RTX 5070 Ti and observed:

| Image | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| Normal OCR photo | Passed | Passed |
| Constructed black-and-white image | EngineCore crashed | Passed |

I’d be happy to contribute the end-to-end test if it would help strengthen this PR. As a minor style suggestion, the commit message is too long maybe.

If that's a hassle, paste the test file here and I'll apply it with a Co-authored-by. And thanks for the commit message note.

<details>

```text
import os

import pytest
import torch
from PIL import Image

from vllm.transformers_utils.processors.deepseek_ocr import (
    ImageTransform,
    dynamic_preprocess,
)


@pytest.mark.core_model
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("model_id", "image_size", "model_env", "load_format"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR",
            640,
            "DEEPSEEK_OCR_TEST_MODEL",
            "dummy",
            id="ocr1",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2",
            768,
            "DEEPSEEK_OCR2_TEST_MODEL",
            "auto",
            id="ocr2",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_deepseek_ocr_balanced_tiled_image(
    vllm_runner, model_id, image_size, model_env, load_format
):
    image = Image.new("RGB", (1536, 768), "white")
    image.paste("black", (768, 0, 1536, 768))

    crops, crop_ratio = dynamic_preprocess(image, image_size=image_size)
    patches = torch.stack([ImageTransform()(crop) for crop in crops])
    assert crop_ratio == (2, 1)
    assert patches.numel() > 0
    assert patches.sum().item() == 0

    model = os.environ.get(model_env, model_id)
    with vllm_runner(
        model,
        max_model_len=2048,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.8,
        load_format=load_format,
    ) as vllm_model:
        outputs = vllm_model.generate_greedy(
            ["<image>\nFree OCR."], max_tokens=8, images=[[image]]
        )

    assert len(outputs) == 1
    assert len(outputs[0][0]) > 0
```

</details>
Added your test as a separate commit with your authorship — thanks for putting it together.

detail.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum patch guard in _encode…

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Guard tests for DeepSeek-OCR _encode_local_features.
+
+_encode_local_features must skip processing only for an empty-element
+patches tensor, not for a zero-sum one.
+
+Regression for #64075: the old guard ``torch.sum(patches).item() == 0``
+returned None for a 1536x768 half-white/half-black image whose two
+normalised crop patches cancel to sum==0, causing a shape mismatch in
+_merge_multimodal_embeddings and a fatal EngineCore crash.
+
+The correct guard is ``patches.numel() == 0``.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_ocr import DeepseekOCRForCausalLM
+from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_ocr2 import DeepseekOCR2ForCausalLM
+
+
+class TestDeepseekOCREncodeLocalFeaturesGuard:
+    def test_ocr2_empty_patches_returns_none(self):
+        """Zero-element tensor → skip local encoding (non-tiled image)."""
+        empty = torch.empty(0, 3, 224, 224)
+        assert DeepseekOCR2ForCausalLM._encode_local_features(None, empty) is None
+
+    def test_ocr2_zero_sum_patches_enters_model_body(self):
+        """Non-empty patches that happen to sum to zero must NOT return None.
+
+        The method will raise AttributeError when it tries to call
+        self.sam_model on a None self – that is the expected outcome here
+        because it proves the guard was passed, not that encoding succeeded.
+        The real crash was a shape-mismatch ValueError that killed EngineCore.
+        """
+        # Two patches that cancel: white (1.0) + black (-1.0) after Normalize.
+        wb = torch.cat([torch.ones(1, 3, 4, 4), -torch.ones(1, 3, 4, 4)])
+        assert wb.numel() > 0
+        assert wb.sum().item() == 0.0
+        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
+            DeepseekOCR2ForCausalLM._encode_local_features(None, wb)
+
+    def test_ocr1_empty_patches_returns_none(self):
+        """OCR-1: zero-element tensor → skip local encoding."""
+        empty = torch.empty(0, 3, 224, 224)
+        crop_shape = torch.tensor([0, 0])
+        assert (
+            DeepseekOCRForCausalLM._encode_local_features(None, empty, crop_shape)
+            is None
+        )
+
+    def test_ocr1_zero_sum_patches_enters_model_body(self):
+        """OCR-1: non-empty zero-sum patches must pass the guard."""
+        wb = torch.cat([torch.ones(1, 3, 4, 4), -torch.ones(1, 3, 4, 4)])
+        crop_shape = torch.tensor([1, 2])
+        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
+            DeepseekOCRForCausalLM._encode_local_features(None, wb, crop_shape)

@@ -499,7 +499,7 @@ def _encode_global_features(self, image_tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
     def _encode_local_features(
         self, patches: torch.Tensor, crop_shape: torch.Tensor
     ) -> torch.Tensor | None:
-        if torch.sum(patches).item() == 0:
+        if patches.numel() == 0:
             return None
 
         local_features_1 = self.sam_model(patches)

@@ -343,7 +343,7 @@ def _encode_global_features(self, image_tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
         return features.view(-1, dim)
